title: Single-degree cancellation of a finite coefficient cone obstruction
statement:
Let $D$ be a commutative Noetherian ring [def-weil-pbc-noetherian-ring], $D\to A$ a homomorphism of commutative rings, and $S$ a commutative finite type $D$-algebra, with a fixed surjection $Q_D=D[x_1,\ldots,x_s]\twoheadrightarrow S$, $s\geq0$ [def-weil-pbc-mv-polynomial-ring]. Put $S_A=S\otimes_D A$ and $Q_A=A[x_1,\ldots,x_s]$. Use ordinary module derived categories [def-weil-abstract-derived-category]. Let $K\in D(S_A)$ and let $L\in D(S)$ have cohomology zero outside a finite interval and finitely generated over $S$ in each degree [def-weil-finitely-generated-module]. Suppose given $\gamma:L\to\operatorname{Res}_S^{S_A}K$. Derived tensor products are computed by K-flat resolutions [def-pc-module-kflat-complex]. Write $\gamma_Q$ for restriction to $Q_D$ and let
$$\theta_Q:Q_A\otimes_{Q_D}^{\mathbf L}\operatorname{Res}_{Q_D}^S L\xrightarrow{1\otimes\gamma_Q}Q_A\otimes_{Q_D}^{\mathbf L}\operatorname{Res}_{Q_D}^{S_A}K\xrightarrow{\mu_K}\operatorname{Res}_{Q_A}^{S_A}K$$
be the derived extension--restriction counit composite in $D(Q_A)$; $\mu_K$ comes from the given scalar action. Let $C_Q$ be its cone [def-weil-triangulated-category]. If $n\in\mathbf Z$, $H^i(C_Q)=0$ for all $i>n$, and $H^n(C_Q)$ is a finitely generated $Q_A$-module, then there exist a commutative finite type $D$-algebra $D'$, a factorization $D\to D'\to A$, and $L'\in D(S')$, $S'=S\otimes_D D'$, with bounded finitely generated cohomology over $S'$, together with $\gamma':L'\to\operatorname{Res}_{S'}^{S_A}K$, such that the cone of
$$A\otimes_{D'}^{\mathbf L}L'\xrightarrow{1\otimes\gamma'}A\otimes_{D'}^{\mathbf L}K\xrightarrow{\mu_K}K$$
in $D(S')$ has $H^i=0$ for every $i\geq n$. In the last display tensor retains the $S'$-action and $\mu_K$ is induced by the given ordinary $A$-action. No map of rings is assumed flat. No pseudo-coherence of $K$, compatibility map from $L$ to $L'$, or conclusion in degrees below $n$ is assumed or asserted.

source.place: Agent-formulated single-degree prerequisite for affine descente in the unnumbered Kiehl paragraph after Tag 0CSD, lemma-flat-proper-pseudo-coherent-direct-image-general. This paragraph does not state or prove the cancellation assertion. Kiehl (1972), Ein Descente-Lemma und Grothendiecks Projektionssatz fuer nichtnoethersche Schemata, primary descente proof WANTED; no numbered theorem is attributed to it.

proof.text: Put $Y=\operatorname{Spec}S$ and use the dg coefficient realization of [def-sfb-dg-coefficient-realization], with $\mathcal B=\mathcal O_Y\otimes_D R_A$, $T=\Phi_D$, and $\widehat K$. Transfer $L,K,\gamma$ to the affine scheme module categories. The affine derived equivalence and the dg comparison identify $f=\nu_D(\gamma):T(L)\to\widehat K$ with precisely $\theta_Q$ after restriction along $Q_D\otimes_D R_A\to\mathcal B$ and the equivalence to $D(Q_A)$. Thus $C=\operatorname{Cone}(f)$ has zero underlying cohomology above $n$, and its degree $n$ cohomology is the specified finite $Q_A$-module. These are comparisons of the actual action counits and cones. We use the same symbols for modules and their affine realizations.

source.place: Agent assembly for the affine prerequisite of the unnumbered Kiehl paragraph after Tag 0CSD (lemma-flat-proper-pseudo-coherent-direct-image-general); uses the existing dg coefficient comparison and finite coherent factorization, not a theorem asserted by that paragraph.

proof.text: The finite-type Noetherian permanence theorem makes $S$ Noetherian. The Noetherian pseudo-coherence criterion applies to $L$, which has bounded finite cohomology. By the definition of ring pseudo-coherence choose a bounded-above finite-free $S$-complex $F$ representing $L$. Let $E=\sigma_{\ge n}F$ be the brutal truncation: it has the same terms and differentials in degrees at least $n$ and zero terms below $n$. It is a bounded finite-free complex, and its inclusion in $F$ is a chain map. Put $N=F/E$, which has zero terms above $n-1$. The degreewise short exact sequence gives a distinguished triangle $E\to L\to N\to E[1]$. In particular $E$ is built from finitely many shifts of finite free $S$-modules by its finite brutal filtration.

source.place: Tag 066E (lemma-Noetherian-pseudo-coherent), clause (2); brutal truncation and the short-exact-sequence triangle of derived.tex Tag 0152 (lemma-derived-canonical-delta-functor).

proof.text: The dg comparison makes $T$ exact. Its underlying functor is $A\otimes_D^{\mathbf L}-$, with the $S$-action retained: this is the $E=D$ case of that comparison followed by the affine pullback/tensor identifications. Derived extension preserves an upper cohomological bound, so $UT(N)$ has no cohomology above $n-1$. Also $T(E)$ is perfect over $\mathcal B$: apply $T$ to the finite filtration in step 2; $T(S)=\mathcal B$, and perfection over $\mathcal B$ is closed under finite sums, shifts and cones by its definition.

source.place: Agent assembly for the affine prerequisite of the unnumbered Kiehl paragraph after Tag 0CSD (lemma-flat-proper-pseudo-coherent-direct-image-general); uses the existing dg coefficient comparison and finite coherent factorization, not a theorem asserted by that paragraph.

proof.text: Set $f_E:T(E)\to\widehat K$ equal to $f\circ T(E\to L)$ and put $C_E=\operatorname{Cone}(f_E)$. Apply TR4 to $T(E)\to T(L)\to\widehat K$. Since the cone of the first arrow is $T(N)$, it gives a distinguished triangle $T(N)\to C_E\to C\to T(N)[1]$. Forgetting dg actions preserves this triangle. Its long exact cohomology sequence and step 3 give $H^i(UC_E)\cong H^i(UC)$ for every $i\ge n$. The same argument after the polynomial dg restriction gives $Q_A$-linear isomorphisms. Consequently $H^i(UC_E)=0$ for $i>n$ and $H^n(UC_E)$ has a finite list $z_1,\ldots,z_r$ of $Q_A$-generators. The dg comparison says its action factors through $S_A$, so this list also generates over $S_A$.

source.place: Tag 0145 (definition-triangulated-category), TR4, and Tag 05RS (lemma-cohomology-homological); agent application to the dg coefficient comparison.

proof.text: Use the affine derived equivalence to represent $UC_E$ by an $S$-complex. Choose cycles representing the finitely many $z_j$. Sending the standard basis vectors to these cycles defines a chain map $S^r[-n]\to UC_E$ and hence a morphism $a$ in $D(\mathcal O_Y)$. By the adjunction $T\dashv U$ supplied by the dg comparison, its transpose is $q:P\to C_E$, where $P=T(S^r[-n])=\mathcal B^r[-n]$. The transpose is extension followed by the dg action; therefore $H^n(Uq)$ sends each unit basis vector to $z_j$. Since $R_A$ has zero positive terms, $U\mathcal B$ does also. Its degree-zero cohomology is $\widetilde{S_A}$: the quotient by the degree-zero boundaries is $S\otimes_D(R_A^0/\operatorname{im}d^{-1})=S\otimes_D A$. Thus $H^i(UP)=0$ for $i>n$ and $H^n(UP)=\widetilde{S_A}^{\,r}$; $H^n(Uq)$ is surjective.

source.place: Agent assembly for the affine prerequisite of the unnumbered Kiehl paragraph after Tag 0CSD (lemma-flat-proper-pseudo-coherent-direct-image-general); uses the existing dg coefficient comparison and finite coherent factorization, not a theorem asserted by that paragraph.

proof.text: Let $V=\operatorname{Cone}(q)$. The long exact sequence of $P\to C_E\to V$ shows $H^i(UV)=0$ for $i\ge n$: at $n$ use the surjection in step 5 and $H^{n+1}(UP)=0$; above $n$ both adjacent cohomology groups of $C_E$ and $P[1]$ are zero. Write $\delta:C_E\to T(E)[1]$ for the connecting arrow of $f_E$. Form the homotopy pullback of $\widehat K\to C_E$ along $q$, or equivalently apply TR4 to $q:P\to C_E$ and $\delta:C_E\to T(E)[1]$. It gives an object $H$, a map $u:H\to\widehat K$, and triangles $T(E)\to H\to P\to T(E)[1]$ and $H\xrightarrow{u}\widehat K\to V\to H[1]$. Signs are those of the chosen cone triangles; replacing an attaching map by its negative, if required by rotation, leaves its image unchanged. The first triangle makes $H$ perfect over $\mathcal B$; the second gives $H^i(Uu)$ an isomorphism for $i>n$ and a surjection for $i=n$.

source.place: Tag 0145, TR4 applied to q and the connecting arrow; Tag 05RS. This is one cone attachment, not a claim of functorial cones in a bare triangulated category.

proof.text: Apply [lem-sfb-perfect-coefficient-arrow-finite-realization] to $Y=\operatorname{Spec}S$, the perfect object $H$, the arrow $u$, and $m=n$. The scheme $Y$ is separated and finite type over $\operatorname{Spec}D$: it is a closed subscheme of affine $s$-space via the given presentation. Step 6 verifies its cohomological surjectivity hypothesis. Obtain a finite type $D$-algebra $D'$ factoring to $A$, an object $G$ with bounded coherent cohomology on $Y_{D'}$, a map $\gamma':G\to R\pi_{D'*}K$, and $\sigma:H\to\Phi_{D'}G$ with $\nu_{D'}(\gamma')\sigma=u$ and $H^i(U\sigma)$ surjective for $i\ge n$. This is the existing finite-factorization statement, with its forward arrow and upper-surjectivity clause; no factorization is being taken from its proof.

source.place: Agent assembly for the affine prerequisite of the unnumbered Kiehl paragraph after Tag 0CSD (lemma-flat-proper-pseudo-coherent-direct-image-general); uses the existing dg coefficient comparison and finite coherent factorization, not a theorem asserted by that paragraph.

proof.text: Put $v=U\nu_{D'}(\gamma')$. For $i=n$, $H^i(v)H^i(U\sigma)=H^i(Uu)$ is surjective, so $H^n(v)$ is surjective. For $i>n$ the composite is an isomorphism and $H^i(U\sigma)$ is surjective. Its kernel is contained in the kernel of the composite and hence zero. Thus $H^i(U\sigma)$ is an isomorphism, and so is $H^i(v)=H^i(Uu)H^i(U\sigma)^{-1}$. The cohomology long exact sequence now gives $H^i(\operatorname{Cone}(v))=0$ for all $i\ge n$: the adjacent terms are the cokernel of $H^i(v)$ and the kernel of $H^{i+1}(v)$.

source.place: Tag 05RS and Definition 0147; elementary kernel/cokernel argument for the forward finite factorization.

proof.text: Identify $Y_{D'}=\operatorname{Spec}S'$ and let $L'=R\Gamma(Y_{D'},G)$ under the affine derived equivalence. The ring $S'$ is finite type over the Noetherian ring $D$, so it is Noetherian. Coherence is equivalent to quasi-coherence of finite type on this affine Noetherian scheme; the affine finite-type criterion then makes each $H^i(L')$ a finite $S'$-module, with the bounds of $G$. The affine equivalence and t-exact affine pushforward identify $\gamma'$ with a map $L'\to\operatorname{Res}_{S'}^{S_A}K$. The dg comparison identifies $v$ with the pushforward to $Y$ of the stipulated action-normalized sheaf arrow. The affine pullback/tensor formulas identify that arrow with $A\otimes_{D'}^{\mathbf L}L'\xrightarrow{1\otimes\gamma'}A\otimes_{D'}^{\mathbf L}K\xrightarrow{\mu_K}K$. Indeed their adjoint transposes both apply the given $\gamma'$ and then multiplication by the actual $A$-action; uniqueness in the derived adjunction fixes the map. Affine pushforward detects cohomological bounds, so step 8 gives the required cone vanishing in $D(S')$.

proof.text: The construction works for $r=0$: take $P=0$, so $V=C_E$ and the same triangles and factorization apply. It also works when $E=0$ (if $n$ exceeds the upper support of $F$), for $K=0$, for $s=0$, and for the zero ring. The argument uses only upper bounds under derived tensor; it never assumes flatness or discards negative Tor groups. No map from $L$ to the final $L'$ was required; the auxiliary perfect object is the one to which the finite-factorization theorem applies.
